Composite Materials Applied Field Standard Principle 2: Use composite materials to complete Principle 2: When you join pieces of fiberglass reinforcement to form a seam, overlap the pieces by 1 to 3 inches (p. 60).
Composite Materials Applied Field Standard Principle 3: Use composite materials to complete Principle 3: This ensures that the structural properties of the laminate are not weakened (p. 60).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Composite Materials Applied Field Standard): Step 1 (Use composite materials to complete): When you saturate the fiberglass reinforcement with resin, air can be trapped in the laminate, creating voids (p. 60).

Step 2 (Composite Materials Applied Field Standard): Step 2 (Use composite materials to complete): Air voids aresimply bubbles, which when trapped in the cured laminate cancause problems ranging from poor appearance to structuralfailure (p. 60).

Step 3 (Composite Materials Applied Field Standard): Step 3 (Use composite materials to complete): To remove air bubbles, use a squeegee or a paint roller to push the saturated glass reinforcement evenly down to themold surface, squeezing air (p. 60).
Step 4 (Composite Materials Applied Field Standard): Step 4 (Use composite materials to complete): Temperature is important in properly curing resins (p. 60).
